title: Nonreduced fibres detected by free annihilator and principal quotients
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq X$ an affine open subscheme whose structure map comes from the specified $A$-algebra structure on the commutative ring $B$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $b\in B$ satisfy $b^n=0$ for some $n\geq1$. Put $C=B/\operatorname{Ann}_B(b)$, where $\operatorname{Ann}_B(b)=\{x\in B:bx=0\}$, and $D=B/bB$. Assume $C\ne0$ and both $C$ and $D$ are free $A$-modules [def-weil-pbc-free-module], with possibly infinite bases. Then, for every homomorphism $A\to k$ to a field, $b\otimes1$ is a nonzero nilpotent element of $B\otimes_Ak$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. Consequently, for every $t\in\operatorname{Spec}A$ the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_t$ is not reduced [def-pc-scheme-fibre, def-pc-reduced-scheme]. No domain, finite type, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $A$, $B$, or $f$.

proof.text: Put $I=\operatorname{Ann}_B(b)$ and let $q:B\to D$ be the quotient map. Multiplication defines an $A$-linear map $j:C\to B$, $[x]\mapsto bx$: changing $x$ by an element of $I$ does not change $bx$. If $j([x])=0$, then $x\in I$, so $[x]=0$. Its image is $bB=\ker q$, and $q$ is surjective. Thus $0\to C\xrightarrow{j}B\xrightarrow{q}D\to0$ is exact.

source.place: Tag 0575, lemma-nonreduced-in-neighbourhood, proof: the short exact sequence and its field base changes; final paragraph on the nonreduced whole fibre

proof.text: Use the assumed freeness of $D$: choose a basis $(d_i)$ and lifts $z_i\in B$ with $q(z_i)=d_i$. The rule $s(\sum a_i d_i)=\sum a_i z_i$ defines an $A$-linear section of $q$, since each expansion is finite and unique. Define $r:B\to C$ by requiring $j(r(x))=x-s(q(x))$; step 1 gives a unique such element and its $A$-linearity. Since $qj=0$, one has $rj=\mathrm{id}_C$. For any $A\to k$, functoriality of module base change gives $(r\otimes_Ak)(j\otimes_Ak)=\mathrm{id}_{C\otimes_Ak}$. Therefore $j_k=j\otimes_Ak$ is injective. This is the elementary split-sequence case of the tensor-exactness argument in Tag 0575; the item assumes the stronger condition that its last term is free.

source.place: Tag 0575, lemma-nonreduced-in-neighbourhood, proof: the short exact sequence and its field base changes; final paragraph on the nonreduced whole fibre

proof.text:
Choose a basis $(c_i)_{i\in J}$ of $C$. Because $C
e0$, $J$ is nonempty. By [lem-weil-pbc-free-module-base-change-free], $(c_i\otimes1)_{i\in J}$ is a basis of $C\otimes_Ak$ over the nonzero field $k$, so $C\otimes_Ak
e0$. Write $b_k=b\otimes1$. If $b_k=0$, then on every pure tensor one has $j_k([x]\otimes a)=bx\otimes a=(x\otimes a)b_k=0$. Pure tensors generate the tensor product additively, so $j_k=0$, contradicting its injectivity and nonzero source. Hence $b_k
e0$. Also $b_k^n=b^n\otimes1=0$. This proves the asserted nonzero nilpotent for every field map.

source.place: Tag 0575, lemma-nonreduced-in-neighbourhood, proof: the short exact sequence and its field base changes; final paragraph on the nonreduced whole fibre

proof.text: Fix $t\in\operatorname{Spec}A$ and apply step 3 to its canonical residue-field homomorphism $A\to\kappa(t)$. Let $i:X_t\to X$ be the fibre projection and $V=i^{-1}(U)$, an open subset by continuity. Apply [lem-sbc-affine-fibre-sections-tensor] with $R=A$ and the affine open $U$: its section algebra $\Gamma(X,U)=B$ has exactly the specified $A$-algebra structure by hypothesis. Its ring isomorphism $\Gamma(X_t,V)\cong B\otimes_A\kappa(t)$ carries the restriction of $b$ to $b\otimes1$. Thus $\Gamma(X_t,V)$ contains a nonzero nilpotent. The open-section characterization in [def-pc-reduced-scheme] now rules out reducedness of $X_t$. This works for each $t$, without any domain, finiteness or Noetherian assumption.
